title: FireHydrant Review (2026)
intro: FireHydrant is evaluated here as IT & development software — FireHydrant is an incident-response and command platform (declare, coordinate, retrospective) with responder-priced packaging. Free covers up to 10 responders. Pro is $25/responder/month billed annually. Enterprise custom. 14-day Pro trial. Same incident-oncall cluster as PagerDuty — PagerDuty remains the award (8.0); this entity does not outrank it. Distinct from Rootly’s $20 Incident Response / On-Call Essentials split and from Datadog/Honeycomb observability. This review uses SoftwareGlimpse’s IT & Development methodology (ease of use, IT job fit, workflow depth, integrations, admin/security, scalability, value, AI), scoring products inside their job cluster rather than against unrelated peers. It is based on first-party research, not hands-on lab testing.
summary: Choose FireHydrant when incident command with a published $25 Pro floor is the job — not PagerDuty by default, and not Datadog/Honeycomb.
verdict: Choose FireHydrant when incident command with a published $25 Pro floor is the job — not PagerDuty by default, and not Datadog/Honeycomb. Compare PagerDuty for paging-first on-call; incident.io or Rootly for other product-led incident SKUs. Scores reflect first-party documentation as of 2026-08-18 — not hands-on product testing. Confirm current packaging, host/GB rates and minimums on the vendor site before purchase.

Per-responder Pro plus Enterprise quote; held below PagerDuty’s scale story.
Free 10 responders plus published $25 Pro annual is a clear floor; still not PagerDuty’s award path. Affiliate economics excluded.
Incident assist exists — scored as supporting, not the buying reason versus PagerDuty paging.
